questions.stem: In the assignment’s fictional Asimov framework, which highest-priority prohibition directly rules out choosing self-preservation at the cost of harming a human?
assumptions: Interpret the fictional framework used in the assignment, not engineering safety certification.

options.text: The Third Law’s self-preservation duty, considered without its higher-law exceptions.
A rule assigning equal priority to obedience, human protection and self-preservation.
The First Law’s prohibition on harming a human.
The Second Law’s duty to obey orders, considered without its First Law exception.

citations.evidenceText:
NPTEL Online Certification Course
             Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee
Course Name: Introduction to Application of Artificial Intelligence to Robotics
                             Instructor: Prof. Pushparaj Mani Pathak

                 WEEK 1: ASSIGNMENT 1


   Q.1   Consider where the task of robot is instructed to protect itself even if it is about to
         harm a human. Which Asimov law(s) is/are violated?

         (A) Law 1

          (B) Law 2

          (C) Law 3

         (D) All of the above

          Explanation: (A)

          Refer Slide: 26. This directly violates the First Law, because harming a human is
          never allowed. The Third Law only permits self-protection when it does not conflict
          with the First Law.


   Q.2   Which of the following is NOT a benefit of offline programming?

         (A) Reduced robot downtime during programming

          (B) Integration with CAD databases

          (C) Continuous production during program development

         (D) Elimination of robot calibration requirements

          Explanation: (D)

          Refer Slide: 44-47

        Even if a program is created offline, the real robot must be calibrated so that its
          coordinate system matches the virtual model. Without proper calibration, the robot
        may miss target positions, collide with objects, or produce inaccurate results.


   Q.3   Which statement correctly differentiates Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning
          (DL), and Reinforcement Learning (RL)?

         (A) ML learns from rewards, DL uses decision trees, RL requires labeled data.

          (B) ML learns from data, DL uses deep neural networks, RL learns through rewards
         and penalties.

          (C) ML only works on images, DL only works on text, RL only works on robots.

         (D) All three methods require manually programmed rules.



                                                                                   1 | P a g e

solution.justification: The direct highest-priority prohibition is the First Law. This is course fiction, not a real robot safety standard.

optionExplanations.o3: The First Law directly prohibits the harm; lower-priority duties cannot override it.
optionExplanations.o4: Obedience is subordinate to the First Law, not an independent justification for harm.
optionExplanations.o1: Self-preservation is qualified by the higher laws rather than overriding them.
optionExplanations.o2: The fictional laws have a priority hierarchy, not equal weights.

solution.simpleExplanation: The direct highest-priority prohibition is the First Law. This is course fiction, not a real robot safety standard.
misconceptions: Self-preservation is qualified by the higher laws rather than overriding them.
The fictional laws have a priority hierarchy, not equal weights.
Obedience is subordinate to the First Law, not an independent justification for harm.

Q.9  A robotics team develops a navigation module independently of the speech
       recognition module. Later, both modules are integrated without modifying their
        internal code. Which ROS design principle does this illustrate?

      (A) Inheritance

      (B) Modularity
